title: Unreal past and hypothetical meaning
tagline: Past tense, but not about the past — how English signals 'this isn't real' without a single if.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations (ONLY, IF, RATHER, TIME, WOULD, WHAT)
Reading & Use of English Part 1 — multiple-choice cloze (wish / as if / would rather / suppose)
Writing Part 2 — informal letter or review: expressing regret, irritation and preference
Speaking Part 4 — discussing hypothetical situations and mild complaints
why: C1 candidates need to sound natural when nothing they're saying is literally true: a regret, a complaint about someone else's habits, a polite request that isn't really about the past at all. This whole family of structures — wish, if only, as if, would rather, it's time, suppose — reuses the past tense to mark distance from reality, and Use of English tests the fine grammar (which tense, whose subject) that native speakers apply almost without thinking.

diagrams.title: Wish and if only across three times

marks.label: if only I hadn't shouted at him
marks.sub: wish/if only + past perfect: regret about the past

marks.label: if only I spoke French
marks.sub: wish/if only + past simple: a present state I want to be different

marks.label: if only it would stop raining
marks.sub: wish/if only + would: something I want to change

arrows: different tense, same distance from reality
diagrams.caption: Wish and if only always borrow a past form, but which past form depends entirely on which timeline the regret belongs to.

diagrams.title: as if / as though: same time or earlier?

rows.label: Meaning
cells: an unreal or doubtful situation at the same time
an unreal or doubtful situation that happened earlier

rows.label: Example
cells: She talks as if she knew the answer already.
She looked as if she'd seen a ghost.

rows.label: Could be true?
cells: often genuinely doubtful, sometimes just informal
almost always presented as unreal or exaggerated

rows.label: Typical verbs
cells: look, sound, feel, talk, act + as if
look, sound, feel + as if (looking back)

diagrams.title: would rather / sooner + a different subject

parts.chip: a preference about someone else's action

diagrams.caption: When the preference is about a different subject, would rather switches to a past tense, even though the meaning is present or future.

formula.ex: wish / if only / as if / would rather / it's time / suppose

formula.chip: a present, past or hypothetical meaning — never a real past action

head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: a present situation I want to be different
an unreal or doubtful situation, same time
she acts as if she owned the place
as if / as though + past perfect
an unreal or doubtful situation, earlier time
he looked as if he'd run a marathon
a preference about someone else's action
criticism that something should already be happening
a hypothesis, often about the present or future

use.point: Wish and if only across the three times

examples.text: I wish I had studied harder for the mocks — now I'm paying for it.
examples.note: wish + past perfect = regret about the past

examples.text: If only we lived closer to the coast.
examples.note: if only + past simple = a present state I want to be different
wish + past simple (subjunctive were) for a near-future wish

use.point: As if / as though for unreal or doubtful comparisons

examples.text: Liam answered every question as if he had written the exam himself.
examples.note: as if + past perfect = an unreal comparison about something earlier

examples.text: She looked at me as though I had two heads.
examples.note: as though + past simple = an unreal comparison happening now

examples.text: He spends money as if he were a millionaire.
examples.note: as if + were (subjunctive) for a hypothetical comparison

use.point: Would rather/sooner for someone else's actions; it's (high/about) time

examples.text: I'd rather you didn't mention this to Miss Vega just yet.
examples.note: would rather + past for a preference about someone else, present/future meaning

examples.text: I'd sooner she had told me the truth from the start.
examples.note: would sooner + past perfect for a preference about the past

examples.text: It's high time the council fixed that broken streetlight.
examples.note: it's (high) time + past for overdue criticism

use.point: Suppose/supposing/what if for hypotheses; wish + would for irritation

examples.text: Suppose the exam board changed the syllabus next year — would you still apply?
examples.note: suppose/what if + past for a hypothesis about the future

examples.text: I wish the neighbours'd stop playing music at midnight.
examples.note: wish + would for irritation at someone else's behaviour

watch_out.wrong: I wish I know the answer.
watch_out.why: A present wish needs the past simple (the unreal past), not the present.

watch_out.wrong: I wish I would be taller.
watch_out.why: Wish + would doesn't describe your own state — use the past simple/subjunctive for wishes about yourself.

watch_out.wrong: She talks as if she was knowing everything.
watch_out.why: Know is a stative verb — it doesn't take the continuous, even in the unreal past.
After would rather + a different subject, use the past simple, even though the meaning is present or future.
It's (high/about) time is followed by the past simple, not the base form.

watch_out.wrong: I wish you stop making that noise.
watch_out.right: I wish you'd stop making that noise.
watch_out.why: Wish + would (not the bare present) expresses irritation at someone else's behaviour.

dialogue.title: Regrets and requests
dialogue.context: The group project is going badly, and Miss Vega finds the four students blaming each other and wishing they'd done things differently.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: You all look exhausted. What's going on?

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: I wish I'd started the project earlier — now I'm up until midnight every night.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Same here. If only we'd divided the work properly from the start.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Honestly, Mateo acts as if he were doing this all alone.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: That's not fair! I'd rather you didn't say that in front of everyone.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Calm down, both of you. It's high time this group sorted its problems out.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: She's right. Suppose I gave you an extra two days — would that help?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: That would help enormously, thank you.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: I still wish Mateo'd just listen when we suggest ideas.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Fine. I'd sooner we agreed on a plan right now than keep arguing.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Good. And what if we met tomorrow at lunch to finish the slides?

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Perfect. Let's stop wishing and start working.

items.sentence: I wish I ___ more time to prepare for the interview.
items.why: a present wish needs the past simple

items.sentence: If only she ___ me the truth before I found out myself.
items.why: if only + past perfect = regret about the past

items.sentence: He talks ___ he owned the whole company.
items.why: as if introduces an unreal comparison

items.sentence: I'd rather you ___ that story to the new students.
items.why: would rather + a different subject + past simple

items.sentence: It's about time the school ___ the broken lift.
___ you lost your phone right now — what would you do?
I wish the dog ___ barking at three in the morning.
items.why: wish + would expresses irritation at someone else's behaviour

items.second_end: her how I felt at the time.

summary: Wish and if only borrow the past tense to talk about now (past simple), the past (past perfect) and what you want to change about someone's behaviour (would).
As if / as though + past (or past perfect) presents a comparison as unreal or doubtful, not as a fact.
After would rather/sooner with a different subject, switch to the past simple, even though the meaning is present or future.
It's (high/about) time + past simple is a polite but pointed way of criticising a delay.
Suppose, supposing and what if introduce a hypothesis with the same unreal-past logic as a conditional, without needing if.
